title: Wipro Completes Record ₹15,000 Crore Buyback as Q1 Earnings Miss Estimates
excerpt: India's fourth-largest IT exporter returned $1.6 billion to shareholders through its largest-ever tender offer, but a revenue miss and margin contraction raise questions about its competitive position.
body:
• Wipro's Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹244.79 billion ($2.54 billion) missed analyst estimates, while net profit rose just 0.6% to ₹33.52 billion.
  • The company completed its largest-ever share buyback of ₹15,000 crore ($1.6 billion) at ₹250 per share, repurchasing 5.7% of its equity capital.
  • Operating margins contracted to 16% from 17.3% a year ago, with the company warning of near-term margin volatility amid salary hikes and deal ramp-ups.
  • Total deal wins fell sharply to $3.37 billion from $5 billion a year earlier, with weakness concentrated in the Americas healthcare segment.

Q1 Earnings Fall Short of Street Expectations

Wipro Limited reported a mixed first quarter for fiscal year 2027, with revenue rising 10.6% year-over-year to ₹244.79 billion ($2.54 billion) but missing the analyst consensus estimate of ₹247.76 billion. Net profit edged up a modest 0.6% to ₹33.52 billion, falling short of the ₹34.42 billion that markets had anticipated.

The results, announced on July 16, sent Wipro's U.S.-listed shares down as much as 2.2% in pre-market trading and underscored the challenge facing CEO Srinivas Pallia as he attempts to revive growth at India's fourth-largest IT services exporter.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=I6l6J1s_OVM

"Wipro is lagging its peers. It's possible that the type of legacy deals that Wipro has is not able to generate sustaining growth."

— Piyush Pandey, Analyst, Centrum Broking

The Bengaluru-based company guided second-quarter revenue at $2.57 billion to $2.63 billion, implying a sequential decline of 1.5% to growth of 0.5% — narrower than the -1% to +1% range analysts had expected. Total deal wins for the quarter fell sharply to $3.37 billion from $5 billion a year earlier.

Margin Pressure and Americas Weakness

Wipro's operating margin contracted 130 basis points year-over-year to 16%, down from 17.3% in both the preceding quarter and the year-ago period. The company attributed the compression to annual salary increments and the ramp-up costs of several large deals signed in recent quarters.

CFO Aparna Iyer warned of "near-term margin volatility" as Wipro invests in employees and strategic growth areas amid a rapidly evolving technology landscape shaped by artificial intelligence.

The Americas market — Wipro's largest geography — declined due to client-specific issues and reduced tech spending in the healthcare segment. The weakness stood in contrast to peers Tata Consultancy Services, HCLTech, and Tech Mahindra, all of which beat quarterly revenue expectations aided by a depreciating rupee and varied segment strength.

Record ₹15,000 Crore Buyback Completed

Alongside the Q1 results, Wipro confirmed the completion of its largest-ever share buyback programme — a ₹15,000 crore ($1.6 billion) tender offer at ₹250 per share that repurchased up to 600 million equity shares, representing approximately 5.7% of the company's paid-up capital.

The buyback, first announced in April during the Q4 FY26 earnings, was executed through the tender offer route with a record date of June 5 and a tendering window from June 11 to June 17. Share extinguishment was completed by July 6, marking Wipro's first buyback since June 2023.

"This is our largest buyback, and we expect to buy back 5.7% of our paid-up capital. Our endeavour has always been to return a substantial portion of the cash generated to our shareholders."

— Aparna Iyer, CFO, Wipro

Iyer noted that Wipro distributed $1.3 billion in dividends during FY26, taking the total payout ratio for the three-year block ending FY26 to 88% — well above the company's stated capital allocation policy. Promoters and promoter group members, who hold approximately 72.6% of Wipro's equity, participated in the buyback.

What It Means for NRI Investors

For NRI shareholders tracking Indian IT stocks through ADRs or direct holdings, the buyback offered an attractive exit at ₹250 per share — a premium of roughly 22.5% over Wipro's trading price at the time. However, the revised tax treatment under India's FY26 Union Budget means buyback proceeds are now taxable in the hands of investors, adding a layer of complexity for cross-border shareholders.

The broader concern remains Wipro's competitive positioning. While the company's capital return story is strong, its operational performance trails peers in a sector grappling with cautious client spending and the disruptive potential of AI. Investors will be watching whether Pallia's "services-as-a-software" strategy and recent acquisitions — including the $70.8 million Alpha Net Consulting deal — can translate into sustained revenue acceleration.
nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Indian IT stocks face complex tax treatment on buyback proceeds under new rules, while Wipro's competitive position versus peers like TCS and HCLTech remains a key concern for diaspora portfolios.
